inputs.share_count_basis: 5,415.478m weighted average for H1 FY2026 (interim note 11); the same note states there were no potential ordinary shares in issue, so basic = fully diluted. Held FLAT: the small share-award charge is expensed in the flows (treatment B); the FY2025 RMB50.2m on-market purchase was the award-scheme trustee, not a capital return.
inputs.net_cash_composition: 30 Jun 2026 (interim SoFP + notes 15/16/20), RMB m: bank balances and cash 5,928.7 (incl. time deposits >3m) + other financial assets 3,036.2 (bank CDs 1,538.3, bank fixed-rate notes 722.0, structured deposits 503.4, debt instrument at amortised cost 272.4; all bank-issued, interest-bearing, at amortised cost) + principal-protected bank financial products inside FVTPL 272.5 = 9,237.4; less bank borrowings 2,561.8 (the RMB2,028.9m long-term bonds outstanding at 31 Dec 2025 were repaid in H1 FY2026 and refinanced with bank loans). Excluded: pledged/restricted deposits 146.8, FVTOCI 126.6, lease liabilities 3,346.7 (treatment B). Private-fund and equity investments at FVTPL (1,632.6) are carried in equity_bridge instead, because their fair-value gains sit outside the core-operating EBITDA used here.
inputs.owner_fcf_derivation: last_fcf = reported_fcf 3,991.6 (OCF 5,664.2 - PP&E capex 1,672.6) - SBC 58.8 - interest income 270.7 - lease payments classified in financing 1,023.8 = 2,638.3. The RMB186.0m lease interest is inside the 1,023.8 financing line (finance costs 238.2 are added back in full in OCF, and the separate 'Interest paid' 50.1 equals bond 46.0 + bank 5.4 interest), so it is not deducted a second time. Short-term/variable lease payments (~RMB203m, the remainder of the RMB1,227.3m 'total cash outflow for leases') are already expensed inside EBITDA.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 AR consolidated cash flow statement, 'Share-based payment expense' RMB58,753k (file 6862.HK_Annual_FY2025.txt:8058); FY2024 1,368k, FY2023 958k; H1 FY2026 1,040k. No net-share-settlement taxes disclosed (EquityAwardTaxes 0). The FY2025 figure is the launch year of the 2025 share award scheme and H1 FY2026 is back at ~RMB1m, so the forward path is carried at 0% with the historical charge visible here.
inputs.buyback_note: FY2025 'Payments on repurchase of shares' RMB50.2m = trustee purchases for the share award scheme, not a capital-return programme. H1 FY2026 nil. Historically the company returns cash via dividends (FY2025 RMB4,133m, FY2024 RMB6,071m incl. special).
inputs.fx_note: Statements and all flows in RMB (CNY); HKEX quote in HKD. CNY->HKD 1.1747 from Yahoo CNYHKD=X at 2026-10-23 (regularMarketTime 1792773686). No dual listing exists for a parity check; the HKD-declared interim dividend (HKD0.377/share) is the company's own translation and is consistent with ~1.17-1.18. Per-share values are computed in CNY and converted to HKD for the unsuffixed intrinsic_value / weighted_iv so they compare to current_price; CNY twins carried with suffix.
inputs.wacc_rationale: Built in CNY, the currency of the flows: China 10y CGB ~1.8% risk-free + 1.1 beta x 6.5% China equity risk premium = 9.0% cost of equity; bank debt is immaterial (RMB2.6bn at ~2-3%) against a net-cash balance sheet so WACC ~ CoE = 9.0%. Same rate in all three scenarios: cyclicality, the SSS decline and execution risk are charged in the scenario flows and weights, not stacked on the discount rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: (B) Leases as operating cost. The lease cash classified in financing ('Repayments of lease liabilities', principal + lease interest; FY2025 RMB1,023.8m = 2.37% of revenue, FY2024 2.09%) is charged inside EBIT via lease_cost_pct_path at 2.4% of revenue; lease liabilities (RMB3,346.7m at 30 Jun 2026) are EXCLUDED from net debt. da_pct_path is D&A ex right-of-use depreciation (FY2025 total D&A 2,182.1 less ROU depreciation 742.7 = 1,439.3 = 3.33% of revenue) so the lease is not charged twice in the tax line. Cash-basis lease charge exceeds the P&L ROU charge (743 + 186) by ~RMB300m because the lease book is amortising faster than it is renewed; the cash figure is used deliberately.
inputs.nci_treatment: Non-controlling interests are immaterial (RMB -8.8m equity at 31 Dec 2025, RMB -7.9m share of profit). No deduction; flows are treated as 100% attributable.
inputs.ebitda_basis: EBITDA margin path is post-IFRS-16 CORE operating EBITDA = core operating profit + total D&A, EXCLUDING interest income, fair-value gains and other non-operating items. FY2025: 5,403.2 + 2,182.1 = 7,585.3 = 17.5% of revenue (FY2024: 6,230 + 2,558.5 = 20.6%; H1 FY2026: 2,513.5 + 907.9 = 15.3% vs H1 FY2025 17.2%). The Metrics.csv 'EBITDA' (8,232 / 19.0%) includes interest income and other gains and is NOT the basis here.
inputs.fy0_calibration: Component build at FY2025 drivers: 17.5% EBITDA - 2.37% lease - 0.14% SBC - 3.33% D&A = EBIT 11.7% (RMB5,040m) vs statutory PBT ex interest income 5,541m and core OP less lease interest 5,217m; 30% cash tax (paid 1,811.4 / PBT 5,811.7 = 31.2%; FY2024 26.8%) -> NOPAT ~3,530 + D&A 1,439 - capex 1,673 = ~3,300 with zero working capital, against actual owner FCF 2,638 after a ~RMB-640m working-capital outflow (other payables and contract liabilities fell as revenue stalled). The FY2025 WC drag is not carried forward (wc_capture 0 in base and bear).
inputs.notes: FRESH BUILD (no prior DCF). Model: owner-FCF DCF, component route, 10-year horizon, routed via dcf-methods SKILL.md row 'operating company, non-US/cyclical: consumer' with owner-fcf-adaptations (a) currency CNY/HKD, (b) lease treatment B, (e) near-SBC-zero, (f) risk charged once. Haidilao is a self-operated restaurant chain (1,290 self-operated + franchised Haidilao-brand stores plus ~200 sub-brand stores at 30 Jun 2026) whose value is a stream of restaurant cash flow, so the owner-FCF engine applies. Operations outside Greater China were spun off as Super Hi (9658.HK) in Dec 2022/Jan 2023, so FY2021 and earlier revenue is not comparable; FY2022 onward is the continuing perimeter. The business is maturing: same-store sales -6.7% FY2025 and -1.3% H1 FY2026, table turnover 4.1x -> 3.9x/day, guest visits -7.5% FY2025; growth is now coming from delivery (+121% H1 FY2026, 9.2% of revenue, lower margin) and sub-brands, not the core dine-in brand. The build therefore starts from the compressed H1 FY2026 margin, not the FY2023-24 peak, and uses a 15x terminal cap. The 10-year horizon is used because margins in all three scenarios are still moving in year 5. Interest income is stripped because net cash (RMB6.7bn) is ~2.5x the owner-FCF base. The flat share count is funded: the company pays out ~100% of profit as dividends and SBC is negligible.
inputs.terminal_cap_note: 15x owner FCF cap (method range 12-15x for structurally slower businesses). Current EV/owner-FCF at the market price is ~ (HKD50.0bn / 1.1747 - 6.7bn net cash - 1.6bn investments) / 2.64bn = ~13x, so the 15x cap sits just above today's multiple. The cap binds in all three scenarios (Gordon at 9%/2.5% would be 15.8x), i.e. the model does not assume multiple expansion beyond today's.

equity_bridge.item: Private-fund and equity investments at FVTPL (fair value, 30 Jun 2026)
equity_bridge.note: Interim note 16: private fund investments 1,613.0 + unquoted equity 12.9 + quoted equity 6.7. Their fair-value gains/losses are outside the core-operating EBITDA used in the flows, so the asset is added once here at carrying (fair) value. Principal-protected bank products (272.5) are in net cash instead.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: judgment: base-path mid-horizon rate. Equity/revenue/EPS CAGRs are all distorted and none is usable as a forward anchor (see notes).
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: EPS 3yr CAGR (44%) diverges >30% from equity (10%) and revenue (12%) CAGRs because FY2022 is a COVID-lockdown/'Woodpecker'-closure trough and the only year on the continuing (ex-Super Hi) perimeter before FY2023. 5yr figures straddle the Super Hi spin-off and the FY2021 loss, so they are not comparable either. Equity 5yr CAGR is ~0 because the company pays out ~100% of profit.
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF series (reported FCF - SBC - interest income - lease payments in financing), RMB m: FY2022 4,138 -> FY2023 7,339 -> FY2024 5,059 -> FY2025 2,638. The 3yr owner-FCF CAGR (-14.0%) is below the reported-FCF CAGR (-9.2%): interest income grew with the cash pile (121 -> 271) and lease payments drifted up, so an increasing share of reported FCF is non-operating or owed to landlords. FY2025 is also depressed by a ~RMB640m working-capital outflow and a step-up in capex (1,673 vs 452 in FY2023). Revenue growth has decelerated to +1.1% FY2025 / +7.9% H1 FY2026 (delivery-driven).

base.growth_rationale: FY2026 +6%: H1 was +7.9% on delivery (+121%) and sub-brands (+113%) against core dine-in -4%; H2 comps against a stronger H2 FY2025 delivery base. FY2027 +5% on management's stated acceleration of openings and sub-brand replication, fading to 2.5% terminal as the core brand's unit economics continue to normalise.
base.margin_rationale: Starts at 15.8% (H1 FY2026 core EBITDA 15.3%, seasonally similar to FY) vs 17.5% FY2025 and 20.6% FY2024: delivery mix (platform fees), raw-material inflation (37.9% -> 40.5% of revenue) and price-led competition are structural. Recovers only 0.7pp over 5 years from middle-office cost consolidation and the exit of 85 underperforming stores; never regains the FY2023-24 level.
base.capex_rationale: FY2025 PP&E capex 3.9% of revenue (FY2024 3.0%, FY2023 1.1% post-closure trough). 2027-28 openings acceleration and ageing-store refurbishment push it to 4.5%, easing to 3.7% at maturity, slightly above D&A ex-ROU (3.4%) consistent with 2.5% unit growth.
base.tax_rationale: 30% cash rate: PRC 25% statutory plus 5-10% withholding on the near-100% dividend payout from PRC subsidiaries and non-deductible items; FY2025 paid/PBT 31.2%, FY2024 26.8%, provision/PBT 30.5% FY2025.

bull.rationale: Same-store sales stabilise in FY2027 as the industry's 'rational competition' phase holds; food-stall hot pot and sushi formats replicate at scale, delivery keeps compounding, and openings accelerate in 2027-28. Core EBITDA margin recovers to 18.5% - still 2pp below FY2024 - as the middle office takes cost out and delivery scale dilutes platform fees. Growth brings modest negative-working-capital cash (5% capture: payables + contract liabilities exceed receivables + inventory).

bear.rationale: The core dine-in decline does not stabilise: table turnover keeps sliding, guest visits fall faster than new units add, delivery growth slows as platforms re-price subsidies, and the sub-brand rollout stalls as it did in the 2022 'Woodpecker' cycle. Revenue is flat-to-down FY2027-29 with another round of store closures; core EBITDA margin settles at 13.5% as raw-material and labour costs cannot be passed through. Capex falls to a maintenance 3.0%. The company stays net cash and keeps paying dividends - this is an eroding franchise, not a solvency case.

scenario_narratives.base: Haidilao is a mature, cash-generative restaurant chain whose core dine-in brand is shrinking slowly while delivery and sub-brands fill the gap at lower margin. Revenue grows mid-single digits for two years on openings and delivery, then fades to 2.5%. Core EBITDA margin starts from the compressed H1 FY2026 run-rate (15.3%) and recovers less than 1pp. Capex steps up for the 2027-28 opening and refurbishment cycle, then normalises. The RMB6.7bn net cash pile and RMB1.6bn fund investments are added once, with interest income stripped from the flows.
scenario_narratives.bull: The axes that have to go right: SSS stabilisation in 2027, successful replication of the two proven sub-brand formats, delivery continuing to compound without margin dilution, and the middle-office reorganisation actually lowering unit costs. Core EBITDA margin recovers to 18.5% and revenue compounds ~5.5% over the decade.
scenario_narratives.bear: The axes that go wrong: structural traffic decline in hot pot dine-in, price-war competition and platform re-pricing, and a second failed diversification cycle. Revenue stagnates, margins compress to 13.5%, capex drops to maintenance. The balance sheet means this is a slow erosion of value, not distress; the dividend is cut with earnings.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% default to 30% because the thesis rests on an unproven pivot (delivery + sub-brands replacing a core brand with three consecutive years of SSS and turnover decline, and H1 FY2026 margins still compressing). Bull cut to 20% because it needs four independent things to go right (SSS stabilisation, sub-brand scaling, delivery margin, middle-office cost-out). No corporate action is live, so the three-scenario frame holds.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Value Haidilao as a mature, net-cash restaurant operator on owner FCF after SBC, lease cash and stripped interest income, starting from the current compressed margin rather than the FY2023-24 peak, with a 15x terminal cap and a bear-heavy weighting. The investment case is the cash yield and balance sheet, not re-acceleration: the price is tested against what the business earns if the core brand merely stops shrinking, and against what it is worth if it does not.
key_risks_to_valuation: Same-store sales and table turnover keep falling (-6.7% / 4.1x->3.9x in FY2025) and the delivery/sub-brand growth that offsets it is lower margin
H1 FY2026 core EBITDA margin compressed ~2pp YoY (raw materials 37.9% -> 40.5% of revenue, platform fees); the base case assumes only a partial recovery
Execution risk of reorganising the middle office, scaling two sub-brands, and accelerating openings simultaneously; the 2022 'Woodpecker' closure cycle is the precedent
Cash-basis lease charge (2.4% of revenue) is below the IFRS-16 ROU book only because the lease portfolio is amortising; renewal of the 1,300-store estate could lift it
RMB/HKD translation: all flows are CNY, the quote is HKD; a 5% CNY depreciation moves every HKD per-share value by ~5%
30% cash tax rate embeds dividend withholding tax on the near-100% payout; a lower payout would lower the cash rate but also the yield argument
Related-party procurement (Yihai International and other Zhang Yong entities) and the RMB1.6bn private-fund portfolio carried at fair value
